clue.text: Hide jam without hesitation

parts.note: to jam a mechanism is to lock it so it will not move
Chambers gives 'without hesitation or delay' as a sense of away, as in 'fire away'

explanation.surface: An instruction to stash the preserves somewhere quickly, no dithering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam' looks like the fruit preserve; here it is the verb meaning to stick fast. AWAY in the sense 'without hesitation' is a less familiar dictionary meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To lock something away is to put it securely out of sight, so the phrase is a synonym for concealing it.

clue.text: Liberal American signed contract and joined up

parts.note: in American usage, to ink a deal is to sign it, so a signed contract was inked

explanation.surface: A US liberal signs on the dotted line and enlists.
explanation.definitionFit: Linked means connected or joined together, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Cloth that makes prince cold at first, not hot

indicators.note: the letter for cold goes at the start in place of the letter for hot

parts.note: Hamlet is Shakespeare's Prince of Denmark
H is the tap abbreviation for hot
C is the tap abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: A fabric that leaves a prince feeling chilly rather than warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Camlet is a fabric, historically made of camel hair or angora and later of wool and silk.

clue.text: Lawsuit father's taken out of proportion

indicators.note: taken out of says the father's letters are removed from the longer word

parts.note: a fraction is a proportion of a whole
FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A legal case in which a father is excluded from a share.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action is a lawsuit brought in court, so the words are synonyms in law.

clue.text: Stifle venomous individual having dislike about unknown team

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

indicators.note: the dislike word goes about, so wraps around, the unknown and the team

parts.note: hate is strong dislike
Y is an algebraic unknown
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a football or cricket team

explanation.surface: A poisonous person who loathes some anonymous team wants to smother it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the dislike around the unknown and the team. Y is the algebra convention for an unknown; a team of eleven is XI in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To asphyxiate is to suffocate, cutting off air, which is what stifle means.

clue.text: Tree snake about to pierce tailless young animal?

indicators.note: to pierce something is to go into it, so one piece is put inside the other
an animal without its tail loses its final letter

parts.note: a baby is a young animal

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the snake's word round to face the other way

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake

explanation.surface: A snake menacing a young creature that has lost its tail: a jungle drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the snake round before 'to pierce' puts it into the docked young animal; the question mark admits a baby is a loose name for a young animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The baobab is a huge African tree with a swollen trunk, a straightforward example of the defining category.

clue.text: Element of expanded account?

parts.note: account is abbreviated AC; read AC as a chemical symbol and spell it out in full to get the element it stands for

explanation.surface: Part of a longer, fuller story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Element' seems to mean a component of a story; it is a chemical element, whose symbol Ac is also the abbreviation for account.
explanation.definitionFit: Actinium is the radioactive element with symbol Ac, the same letters as the short form of account.

clue.text: Utterly useless vitamin left in fish

parts.note: vitamin B1 read as B ONE

indicators.note: in puts the letter for left inside the fish

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A supplement put inside a fish proves completely ineffective.
explanation.walkthrough: Vitamin B1 is spelt out as B ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone idle means thoroughly lazy, idle to the bone, and idle can mean ineffective or of no use.

clue.text: Black bird extremely lucky to land on new bridge, for one

indicators.note: in a down answer, landing on something means sitting above it

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a rook is a crow-like bird

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A lucky blackbird alights on a newly built bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Brooklyn names the famous New York bridge, so a bridge is one thing the word can refer to.

clue.text: Using which, fix handle on gear

definitions.text: Using which, fix handle on gear

parts.words: Using which, fix handle on gear
parts.note: handle is slang for a person's name and gear is clothing; the clue describes a label sewn into clothes to show the owner's name, while sounding like mechanical repair

explanation.surface: Instructions for attaching a handle to some machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a mechanic fixing a lever onto a gearbox. Read 'handle' as a name and 'gear' as clothes: it is the label parents sew into school uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A name tape is a printed strip stitched into garments to identify whose they are, which is exactly how the clue reads cryptically.

clue.text: Squiffy fools rolling over floor

indicators.note: rolling over makes the word for fools turn round and be read backwards

parts.note: nits is British slang for idiots
to floor someone is to knock them out, KO in boxing shorthand

explanation.surface: Tipsy idiots tumbling around on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Squiffy and stinko are both informal words for drunk, so they are slang synonyms.

clue.text: Agree with ditching witness in confrontation

indicators.note: ditching means dropping, so the word for witness is removed from the phrase

parts.note: to see eye to eye is to agree
to witness something is to see it

explanation.surface: Coming round to someone's view while dropping a witness in a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agree' looks like the definition but it supplies the full phrase SEE EYE TO EYE; dropping SEE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people eye to eye are face to face, squaring up to each other, so the phrase describes a confrontation.

clue.text: Forensically examine some Shogun pickups

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Investigators analysing a fleet of Mitsubishi Shogun pickup trucks.
explanation.definitionFit: To unpick a problem is to take it apart carefully and analyse every detail, like a forensic investigator.

clue.text: Rest of statement covering Times article

indicators.note: the statement word covers, so wraps around, the other pieces

parts.note: a relation is a narrative or account, a statement of events
X is the multiplication sign, read as times
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: The remainder of a statement about a newspaper piece in The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times article' looks like a newspaper story; it is X for the multiplication sign and A for an article of grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxation is rest and recreation, time spent unwinding.

clue.text: Is former United supporter following leader of band in AC/DC style?

indicators.note: following says the rest comes after the band's leader
the leader of a band is its first letter

parts.note: ex means former
U is the usual abbreviation for United, as in football team names
an ally is a supporter

explanation.surface: Asks whether an ex-Manchester United fan followed the frontman of the rock band AC/DC.
explanation.walkthrough: AC/DC looks like the rock band but is slang for bisexual, from alternating and direct current.
explanation.definitionFit: AC/DC is slang for attracted to both sexes, so doing something in that manner is acting bisexually.

clue.text: Barely is able to get it back with skilful boxing

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the skilful word goes around the rest

parts.note: sly means artful or skilful
can means is able

indicators.note: back says the word it is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A boxer is just about able to win it back with skilful fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' looks like the sport but means enclosing; 'back' reverses 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scantily means only just, sparingly, as in scantily clad, so it can replace barely.

clue.text: Are all points being taken in by right responder?

indicators.note: the points of the compass are taken into the word are

parts.note: N, S, W and E are all four compass points

explanation.surface: A question about whether all the scores are being taken in by the right person.
explanation.definitionFit: An answerer is one who replies, so the noun is a synonym for one who responds.

clue.text: Man finally opening unopened can in port

parts.note: Ben is a man's name

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word
unopened takes off the first letter, the one that would be opened

parts.note: khazi is British slang for a toilet, as can is American slang

explanation.surface: A man finally opens an unopened can while in port.
explanation.walkthrough: KHAZI is British slang for a lavatory, a sense of can.
explanation.definitionFit: Benghazi is a major Mediterranean port city in eastern Libya.

clue.text: Dependent on setting one tax cut, unexpectedly large

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters of these words fall out in a surprising order

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A single unexpected tax reduction turning out to be large.
explanation.definitionFit: Something contextual depends on its context, that is, on the setting or circumstances around it.

clue.text: Poisoned quotes protecting power on the rise

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed
protecting means surrounding, so the quotes word goes round the power letter

parts.note: to quote is to cite

explanation.surface: Toxic share prices shielding power companies as they climb.
explanation.walkthrough: CITES holding P gives CITEPS, which 'on the rise' turns upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A septic wound is infected with bacteria, poisoned in the sense of blood poisoning.

clue.text: Pamper daughters protected by old king

indicators.note: the daughters are protected by being enclosed in the king's name

parts.note: Old King Cole is the nursery rhyme monarch
D is the abbreviation for daughter, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: An old king spoils his daughters by keeping them safe.
explanation.definitionFit: To coddle is to overprotect and indulge someone, the same as to pamper.

clue.text: Mole appearing as grey on ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A small animal looking grey on the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' looks like the burrowing animal but is a harbour wall; 'on' belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a stone breakwater or pier, and a groyne is a low wall built out to sea to check erosion.

clue.text: Eighties cultural trend born around wit

indicators.note: around says the word for born wraps round the word for wit

parts.note: née marks a woman's maiden name, literally born
a wag is a joker or wit

explanation.surface: A fashion of the 1980s that grew up around some piece of humour.
explanation.definitionFit: New Age was the spiritual and alternative movement of crystals and holistic thinking that boomed in the 1980s.

clue.text: Breed with nympho, one frequently on course

parts.note: a breed is a race or strain
goer is British slang for a sexually eager person

explanation.surface: A risqué line about breeding with someone promiscuous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' here is a racecourse, not a course of study.
explanation.definitionFit: A racegoer regularly attends race meetings, so is often found at a racecourse.

clue.text: Raid on manoeuvres?

indicators.note: manoeuvres suggests the letters of these words are moved around into a new formation

explanation.surface: A military raid carried out during field exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also defines: an inroad is a raid, an attack made during military manoeuvres.
explanation.definitionFit: An inroad is a hostile incursion into enemy territory, a raid of the sort armies make.

clue.text: Recess to include unexpected third anniversary

indicators.note: to include means to hold within, so the recess word goes round the rest

parts.note: a bay is a recess in a wall or room, as in a bay window

indicators.note: unexpected suggests the letters of the word turn up in an unforeseen order

explanation.surface: An alcove containing a surprise third wedding anniversary present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpected' scrambles 'third', and 'to include' puts that scramble inside the recess.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthday is the yearly anniversary of the day someone was born.

clue.text: Met base, heartless, insane gangster

parts.note: the Metropolitan Police are based at Scotland Yard, known simply as the Yard

indicators.note: heartless removes the inside of the word, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A violent criminal meeting a crazed bad end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Met' is not the past of meet but London's Metropolitan Police, whose headquarters is Scotland Yard.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yardie is a member of a Jamaican criminal gang, the name coming from Jamaican slang for home.

clue.text: Dutch city school in east Nederland — less than half of it

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

indicators.note: in places the school abbreviation inside the letters that follow
the first four of the country name's nine letters, short of half

explanation.surface: A Dutch city's school in the east of the Netherlands, a portion of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than half of it' takes the first four of Nederland's nine letters, and 'in' puts the school abbreviation inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Enschede is a city in the eastern Netherlands near the German border, an example of the category given.
